perspective:
Christian Mensah’s available information/experienced perspective:

- He is a police officer and knows he can investigate, gather evidence, and look into matters discreetly.
- He has a close childhood friendship with Jonathan. Christian often seeks Jonathan’s advice on personal and professional matters and values his perspective.
- Recently, Christian felt anxious and suspicious that Jonathan was hiding something important. He observed Jonathan acting differently.
- Christian arranged a meeting with Jonathan at their favorite coffee shop and confronted him.
- Christian told Jonathan he felt Jonathan was hiding something. He heard Jonathan say Christian could trust him.
- Christian explained his anxiety and asked Jonathan what was going on.
- Jonathan admitted he had been keeping something from Christian: Jonathan is in some trouble and didn’t know how to tell him.
- Christian felt worried and empathetic. He offered to help and said they could face it together.
- Jonathan told Christian the situation is complicated and he didn’t want to drag Christian into it.
- Christian insisted he couldn’t stand by and asked what Jonathan needed. Jonathan said he could use support and resources and needed to figure a way out of the mess.
- Christian began to believe Jonathan’s trouble might be related to criminal activity. He felt conflicted and concerned, but decided to investigate further without alarming Jonathan.
- Christian asked Jonathan whether the trouble was related to anything illegal. Jonathan said he couldn’t say for sure, that he might have gotten involved with the wrong people, but claimed he did not do anything illegal himself.
- Christian told Jonathan he wanted to make sure he was safe and would look into it discreetly. Jonathan thanked him and said he trusted Christian to handle it carefully.
- Christian’s investigation led him to believe Jonathan is being framed—someone is trying to set Jonathan up. Christian felt determined and protective and decided to clear Jonathan’s name by gathering evidence.
- Christian told Jonathan he had news: he believes Jonathan is being framed. Jonathan asked if he was sure and who would do such a thing. Christian said he wasn’t sure yet, had leads, and would gather more evidence. Jonathan thanked him.
- Christian later found out or came to believe that the real culprit is someone close to both him and Jonathan. He feels betrayed and resolute.
- Christian told Jonathan he found out who is behind it: someone they both know and trust. He said he intends to confront them and bring them to justice.
- Jonathan warned Christian to be careful, saying the person is dangerous, but also said he trusts Christian.
- The provided dialogue/scenarios do not name the real culprit, though Christian states he has found out who it is.
